title: NYT, Economist among publishers joining coalition to curb unpaid AI use
source_used: Reuters (text read on its copy at CNA; the Reuters link was found through Google News)
key_facts: The New York Times, Agence France-Presse and The Economist joined the Standards for Publisher Usage Rights (SPUR) coalition on Monday 12 Oct 2026.

SPUR launched in February and now has more than 80 members across over 20 countries; new members include The Atlantic and Brazil's National Association of Newspapers; founding members include the Financial Times, BBC and Associated Press.
The coalition aims to prevent AI firms from using or profiting from publishers' content without permission; it is funded entirely by its members.
SPUR is developing industry-wide standards and technical systems to help publishers track and control how AI companies use their content and to facilitate licensing.
SPUR recently introduced its Content Telemetry Standard to standardize how AI agents record and report their use of media content.

Earlier this month USA Today and several newspapers it owns sued OpenAI for alleged copyright infringement; OpenAI and Microsoft face similar claims from authors and news organisations including the New York Times.
Rebecca Grossman-Cohen, the New York Times' head of strategic partnerships and chief of staff, said 'Intellectual property protection and technological advancement can and must co-exist'.
Google organic-search referrals to more than 2,500 websites fell 33% globally between Nov 2024 and Nov 2025, per a Reuters Institute report citing Chartbeat.
quote_evidence: The New York Times, Agence France-Presse and The Economist on Monday joined more than 40 publishers in a coalition aimed at preventing AI firms from using or profiting from their content without permission.
The Standards for Publisher Usage Rights (SPUR) coalition, launched in February, now has more than 80 members across over 20 countries.
why_it_matters_hint: More large publishers are lining up to demand control over, and payment for, AI use of their journalism.
